hook.from: Geography > Location, Terrain, Natural resources; Economy > Exports
hook.excerpt: Oceania, island group consisting of nine coral atolls in the South Pacific Ocean, about half way from Hawaii to Australia || low-lying and narrow coral atolls || one of the smallest and most remote countries on earth; six of the nine coral atolls -- Nanumea, Nui, Vaitupu, Nukufetau, Funafuti, and Nukulaelae -- have lagoons open to the ocean; Nanumaya and Niutao have landlocked lagoons; Niulakita does not have a lagoon || Resources: fish, coconut (copra) || Exports: fish (2023)

physicalGeography.excerpt: low-lying and narrow coral atolls || Oceania, island group consisting of nine coral atolls in the South Pacific Ocean, about half way from Hawaii to Australia

climate.excerpt: tropical; moderated by easterly trade winds (March to November); westerly gales and heavy rain (November to March) || severe tropical storms are usually rare, but in 1997 there were three cyclones; low levels of islands make them sensitive to changes in sea level

economy.excerpt: upper middle-income Pacific island economy; extremely environmentally fragile; currency pegged to Australian dollar; large international aid recipient; subsistence agrarian sector; Te Kakeega sustainable development; domain name licensing incomes || Exports: fish (2023) || Industries: fishing

peopleAndCulture.excerpt: Tuvaluan (official), English (official), Samoan, Kiribati (on the island of Nui) || Protestant 92.7% (Congregational Christian Church of Tuvalu 85.9%, Brethren 2.8%, Seventh Day Adventist 2.5%, Assemblies of God 1.5%), Baha'i 1.5%, Jehovah's Witness 1.5%, other 3.9%, none or refused 0.4% (2017 est.) || Tuvaluan 97%, Tuvaluan/I-Kiribati 1.6%, Tuvaluan/other 0.8%, other 0.6% (2017 est.)
